name: Zerahiah
overview: Zerahiah is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Eliehoenai, who accompanied Ezra during the return to Jerusalem. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. Beyond his role as a father, there are no additional notes or distinguishing details recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zerahiah means 'YHWH shines brightly' or 'YHWH has risen like the sun,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the Lord. This proper name emphasizes God's radiant presence and action, though it was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Zerahiah as a descendant of Pahath-moab and explicitly records him as the father of Eliehoenai. These relationships situate him within a genealogical line connected to the community that returned with Ezra. No other family connections are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Zerahiah's significance lies in his connection to the post-exilic community led by Ezra, as his son Eliehoenai was among those who returned to Jerusalem. This link highlights the continuity of faithful families during the restoration period and underscores the importance of genealogical records in preserving the identity and heritage of God's people. Though not a prominent figure himself, Zerahiah's mention roots the narrative in real family lines instrumental to Israel's spiritual renewal.
